# Finance Policy — [Church Name]

**Effective date:** [Date]  
**Approved by:** [Board/elders/authorized governing body]  
**Policy owner:** [Treasurer/Finance Committee]

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy establishes controls for receiving, holding, spending, recording, and reporting the funds of **[Church Name]** (“the Church”). It applies to staff, board members, ministry leaders, volunteers, and anyone handling Church funds or financial records.

The Church will use its funds only for authorized Church purposes and will maintain accurate records of its financial activity.

## 2. Roles and responsibilities

- **Governing body:** Approves the annual budget, this policy, significant unbudgeted commitments, and financial reports. It reviews the Church’s financial position at least [monthly/quarterly].
- **Treasurer/finance lead:** Oversees bookkeeping, reporting, banking, and financial controls; brings material concerns to the governing body.
- **Authorized approvers:** Review and approve payments as set out in Section 5. No one may approve their own reimbursement or payment.
- **Bookkeeper:** Records transactions and maintains supporting documentation. When feasible, this person should not be the sole person approving or reconciling transactions.
- **Ministry and budget owners:** Spend within approved budgets, obtain required approvals, and submit receipts and other documentation promptly.

The governing body will document who has financial authority and review that list at least annually and whenever roles change.

## 3. Budget and spending limits

The governing body will approve an annual budget before the start of each fiscal year. The budget should identify major income and expense categories and responsible budget owners.

Spending must remain within the approved budget and comply with the approval limits below:

| Transaction or commitment | Required approval |
|---|---|
| Up to $[amount] | [Budget owner] |
| $[amount]–$[amount] | [Budget owner and treasurer/second approver] |
| Above $[amount] | [Governing body or designated committee] |
| Unbudgeted spending above $[amount] | [Governing body or designated committee] |
| Contract or recurring commitment above $[amount/term] | [Governing body or designated committee] |

Approvals must be documented in a durable form, such as the accounting system, an approval workflow, or retained email. Spending may not be divided into smaller transactions to avoid an approval limit.

Urgent spending outside the usual process must be reported to [role/body] as soon as practical and documented at the next meeting.

## 4. Income, donations, and restricted funds

All income must be recorded promptly and deposited into a Church-controlled account. Donation records must be handled confidentially and accessible only to authorized people.

Funds designated or restricted for a particular purpose must be tracked separately in the accounting records and used consistently with the donor’s designation and applicable requirements. If a restriction cannot be fulfilled, the matter must be referred to the governing body and handled in accordance with applicable law and professional advice.

The Church will issue donation acknowledgements or receipts when appropriate under applicable requirements. Donor records must not be altered to suggest a different donation date, amount, or purpose.

## 5. Payments, reimbursements, and purchasing

Every payment must have:
- A clear Church purpose and budget category;
- An invoice, receipt, agreement, or other supporting documentation;
- Evidence of required approval; and
- A record of the payee, amount, date, and payment method.

Reimbursements must be submitted within [number] days, with itemized receipts and an explanation of the Church purpose. Reimbursements are not available for personal expenses. The person requesting reimbursement may not approve it.

Payments should be made by traceable methods where practical. Blank checks, shared banking credentials, and signing checks payable to cash are prohibited except for a documented, approved exception.

## 6. Banking and financial access

Church funds must be held in accounts in the Church’s name, not in personal accounts. The governing body will approve account signers and online banking users.

- At least [two] authorized people must be able to review account activity.
- Payment approval and bank reconciliation should be separated where practical.
- Online access must use individual accounts and secure authentication; credentials must not be shared.
- Access must be removed promptly when a person leaves a role.
- New accounts, loans, credit facilities, or changes to account signers require approval from [governing body/authorized role].

## 7. Cash handling

Cash received must be counted and documented by two people when practical. The count record should include the date, amount, purpose, and names of the counters. Cash must be deposited promptly and intact; it should not be used directly to pay expenses.

Any discrepancy, suspected loss, or irregularity must be reported promptly to the treasurer and [governing body/appropriate contact].

## 8. Reconciliation and financial reporting

Bank and credit-card accounts must be reconciled at least monthly. A person who did not initiate or approve the transactions should review the reconciliation where practical.

The treasurer will provide the governing body with financial reports at least [monthly/quarterly], including:
- Actual income and expenses compared with budget;
- Cash and account balances;
- Restricted-fund balances;
- Significant commitments, variances, or unusual transactions; and
- Any known financial control concerns.

Material errors or suspected misuse must be reported promptly and not held until the next routine report.

## 9. Payroll and contractors

Compensation, benefits, reimbursements, and contractor payments must be properly authorized, documented, and processed in accordance with applicable requirements. Changes to compensation must be approved by [governing body/authorized committee], excluding anyone who may personally benefit from the decision.

The Church will maintain appropriate records for employees and contractors and obtain professional advice where worker classification or tax treatment is uncertain.

## 10. Conflicts of interest and related-party transactions

Anyone involved in a financial decision must disclose any personal, family, or business interest that could affect—or appear to affect—their judgment. A person with a conflict must not approve or influence the transaction. The disclosure and decision must be recorded in the minutes or other official record.

Transactions involving a board member, staff member, or related party require advance review and approval by disinterested authorized decision-makers and must be supported by documentation showing the Church’s purpose and the basis for the terms.

## 11. Records, confidentiality, and retention

Financial records must be complete, secure, and available to authorized reviewers. Access to donor, payroll, banking, and other sensitive information must be limited to people who need it for their role.

Records will be retained and securely disposed of according to the Church’s record-retention schedule and applicable requirements. Records relating to an audit, investigation, dispute, or other hold must not be destroyed while that matter is open.

## 12. Review and exceptions

The governing body will review this policy at least annually. Any exception must be approved in advance by [authorized body/person], documented with its reason, and reported to the governing body.

**Adoption record:** Approved by [body] on [date].  
**Next review date:** [Date]
